q: The Univalence Axiom (Voevodsky) states that for types A and B:
opts: (A = B) ≃ (A ≃ B) — paths between types correspond to equivalences (isomorphisms) of types
A = B iff they have the same cardinality
exp: Univalence: equalities of types = equivalences (type isomorphisms). This makes HoTT 'univalent': if A≃B (they are 'the same' up to equivalence), then A=B. Dynamically, this is like Ornstein's theorem: isomorphic Bernoulli shifts ARE equal (as abstract systems).
